name: ox-issue-fix - Ox Alpha works one GitHub issue end-to-end in an isolated worktree
description: Per-issue gauntlet v2 (issue #846): 3 implementation legs x 2 cross-family verification gates, ALWAYS producing a PR. fetch the issue, create a dedicated git worktree, Ox Alpha implements headless, muse-spark verifies adversarially against the ISSUE TEXT, a revise leg resumes the builder session to address findings, muse re-verifies the revised tree, a polish leg makes a final pass, then ship ALWAYS pushes branch + opens a PR whose body embeds both verification verdicts verbatim plus a KNOWN-ISSUES section listing any standing REJECT points - human reviewers inherit the machine's doubts instead of losing them. Designed for a model that is uncapped but SLOW: generous timeouts, volume over token-frugality. Params: issue (number), repo (absolute path to checkout), wt (absolute worktree path - caller chooses location; scripts/ox-tickets.ps1 defaults it to a sibling dir). Cleanup contract: caller owns worktree lifecycle - `git worktree remove <wt>` after the PR merges.

meta.description: Fetch the issue - title, body, labels.

params.command: git worktree add {{params.wt}} fix/issue-{{params.issue}} || git worktree add {{params.wt}} -b fix/issue-{{params.issue}}

meta.description: Idempotent worktree: attach to an existing fix branch or create it fresh - retries and reruns land in a real directory either way.

params.prompt:
You are fixing a GitHub issue in THIS repository (your cwd is a dedicated git worktree - edit freely here).

=== ISSUE #{{params.issue}} ===
{{nodes.fetch.result.stdout}}

=== HOW TO WORK ===
1. Explore first: find the code the issue is about before proposing anything.
2. This repo's coding doctrine lives in skills/program_style.md (negative space programming) and skills/assert_on.md (assert what you know) - read both and follow them. Surgical edits only: touch only what the fix needs.
3. Implement the minimal correct fix.
4. Verify for real: run npx tsc --noEmit; if tests exist near what you changed, run the targeted vitest file(s), not the whole suite.
5. Do NOT commit - a later step handles that. Leave your changes in the working tree.

Reply with: (a) root cause in one sentence, (b) what you changed and why, (c) verification output proof (paste the tail), (d) list of changed files.

meta.description: Implementer leg 1 - Ox Alpha, uncapped/slow, 45 min budget. Works in the isolated worktree.

params.prompt:
You are an ADVERSARIAL verifier (verification gate 1 of 2). Another agent claims to have fixed a GitHub issue in this worktree. Your job is to sink bad work, not to be agreeable.

=== ISSUE #{{params.issue}} ===
{{nodes.fetch.result.stdout}}

=== IMPLEMENTER'S CLAIM ===
{{nodes.implement.result.reply}}

=== VERIFY, IN THIS ORDER ===
1. git status --short && git diff - read the ACTUAL diff yourself; do not trust the claim's description of it.
2. Does the diff actually address the issue's root cause - or a symptom? Would the reported failure now pass?
3. Scope check: any unrelated changes smuggled in? Flag them.
4. Doctrine check: skills/program_style.md + skills/assert_on.md - hidden assumptions, defensive fallbacks for impossible cases, empty catches swallowing real failures.
5. Re-run npx tsc --noEmit yourself. Paste its tail.
6. If tests cover the changed code, run the targeted file.

Reply EXACTLY one of:
APPROVE - <one-line reason>
REJECT - <numbered list of concrete defects, each with file:line>

meta.description: Verification gate 1 - fresh muse-spark instance (cross-family vs ox-alpha builder), judges against issue text + real diff.

params.prompt:
A verifier reviewed your fix:

=== VERDICT (gate 1) ===
{{nodes.verify.result.reply}}

If the verdict starts with APPROVE: change NOTHING, reply exactly 'No changes needed.' Otherwise address EVERY numbered defect, re-run npx tsc --noEmit, and reply with what you fixed per point. Still do not commit.

meta.description: Revise - implementation leg 2, resumes the builder's session so context carries; no-op on APPROVE.

params.prompt:
You are an ADVERSARIAL verifier (verification gate 2 of 2 - the POST-REVISION re-check, issue #846). A builder fixed a GitHub issue, was reviewed, revised its work in response, and you must now judge the FINAL state with fresh eyes.

=== ISSUE #{{params.issue}} ===
{{nodes.fetch.result.stdout}}

=== GATE 1 VERDICT (what the first reviewer demanded) ===
{{nodes.verify.result.reply}}

=== BUILDER'S REVISION SUMMARY ===
{{nodes.fix.result.reply}}

=== VERIFY THE FINAL STATE ===
1. git status --short && git diff - read the actual current diff end-to-end yourself.
2. Were gate-1 defects genuinely fixed, or cosmetically papered over?
3. Any NEW problems introduced by the revision itself?
4. Re-run npx tsc --noEmit. Paste its tail.

Reply EXACTLY one of:
APPROVE - <one-line reason>
REJECT - <numbered list of remaining/new defects, each with file:line>

meta.description: Verification gate 2 - fresh muse-spark instance re-checks the revised tree; closes the shipped-with-REJECT hole (#846).

params.prompt:
Final gate-2 verifier review of your work:

=== VERDICT (gate 2) ===
{{nodes.verify2.result.reply}}

If the verdict starts with APPROVE: change NOTHING, reply exactly 'No changes needed.' Otherwise this is your FINAL implementation leg (leg 3): fix every remaining defect precisely, re-run npx tsc --noEmit, and reply with what you changed per point plus anything you deliberately left unresolved and why. Still do not commit - the next step ships whatever state exists, including known issues if any remain.

meta.description: Implementation leg 3 (final polish) - resumes the builder thread; addresses gate-2 residuals or declares them.

params.prompt:
Ship the fix. You are in an ISOLATED worktree on branch fix/issue-{{params.issue}} - plain git is safe here (this worktree has its own index; you are NOT on the shared checkout, and never push main).

THIS STEP ALWAYS PRODUCES A PR when any change exists - even if verification raised unresolved concerns. Those concerns go INTO the PR body as a KNOWN-ISSUES section so human reviewers inherit them (#846).

1. git status --short - if EMPTY (and no meaningful work occurred), reply NO-CHANGES and stop.
2. git add <each changed path explicitly> - never add -A / add .
3. git commit -m "<type>(<scope>): <what and why>" - conventional, references the root cause. Type is fix unless the issue is clearly refactor/test/docs/chore.
4. git push -u origin fix/issue-{{params.issue}}
5. gh pr create --base main --title "<title>" --body with EXACTLY these sections:
   Fixes #{{params.issue}}

   ## Summary
   <2-4 sentences: root cause, approach, verification>

   ## Machine review trail
   Gate 1: {{nodes.verify.result.reply}}
   Gate 2: {{nodes.verify2.result.reply}}
   Polish: {{nodes.polish.result.reply}}

   ## KNOWN-ISSUES
   <List any standing REJECT points from either gate that remain unresolved after polish, verbatim with file:line. Write 'none' if all gates approved.>

Reply with the PR URL, or NO-CHANGES.

meta.description: Ship - ALWAYS lands a PR carrying both gate verdicts + KNOWN-ISSUES; unconditional by design (#846).
